b101h.text: Last time, we found that a mind map you make yourself helps you remember more than one you only read. And you draw it from memory first.

b201h.text: A little cat is hiding in this video. Can you spot it?

b202m.text: Cats love a quiet corner. Check under the benches!

b203h.text: Lock in first with your fingers. One finger for every point.

b401h.text: Round one! Next Monday, a blank page each. Who draws more of the map, Pip or Basil? Show me your fingers!

b403p.text: Two. Basil will practise pulling it out of his memory. I will only read mine.

b404m.text: Two! Basil will check his map and fix the gaps, every time.

b405b.text: Three! Pip will read his map five times. That's more than my three!

b501h.text: Monday evening. Let's make one together in TheOneApp. Tap Mind Maps, then Make my own mind map.

b502h.text: Pick the chapter, Magnets, and tap Start a new mind map. The middle word is already there.

b503b.text: Poster closed! Two poles: North pole and South pole. Poles together: unlike poles attract, and like poles repel.

b504b.text: Magnetic materials: iron and steel, not copper or aluminium. And a magnet can pull, and push!

b505h.text: Now the check. Tap Mark my mind map.

b506h.text: Look closer. A green tick pops onto every idea. But one big idea from the poster is missing.

b507h.text: Tap Compare with the poster. There it is: Making a magnet. Tap Back to my mind map, and add it in your own words.

b508b.text: Check and fix means you check your map, then add what you missed, such as my Making a magnet branch, with the stroke method!

b509h.text: Mark it again. Every idea is right, and the map is complete!

b512p.text: Then check your map, and fix what you missed.

b601p.text: I made a poster of the steps for our class. Line one: make your own map in TheOneApp. Line two: tap Compare with the poster first, and copy it. Line three: tap Mark my mind map, and fix what you missed.

b602h.text: Showdown! Double points. Pip's poster has one mistake. Line one, two, or three? Show me with your fingers.

b604b.text: Line two! If you look at the poster first, you are copying, not remembering. Memory first, then compare!

b605h.text: Two fingers? Put up two more on your score hand!

b701h.text: Be an idea! Shrink down. Quietly.

b702h.text: You are an idea: like poles repel. You live in a picture of Basil's memory. It looks like a garden full of paths.

b703h.text: A day goes by. Grass starts to grow over your path. On Tuesday, Basil draws his map from memory, and walks the path to find you. Now it is clearer!

b704h.text: Two more days. The grass grows a little. On Thursday, Basil finds you again. The path is wide and easy to find.

b705h.text: There is no real garden in your head. It is a picture of what scientists found.

b802m.text: Space it out means you draw your map again after a few days, not all at once, such as on Tuesday and Thursday, like Basil!

b804b.text: Draw your map again from memory after one day, three days and a week.

b901h.text: Next Monday. A blank page each. Draw the Magnets map from memory!

b902h.text: Pip's page has two branches. Basil's page has all five! The answer is two: Basil. Did you show two fingers? Put one finger up!

b903p.text: Reading it five times felt easy, but it did not stick. Next time, I'm making my own!

c1003.text: Make it yourself! Memory first, then check! One day, three days, a week!

b1101h.text: Show me your score hand! Three fingers? You beat the Buddies. High five!

b1102h.text: Did you spot the cat? It was curled up on the doormat, by the lift!

b1103m.text: Here is a fun fact! A pet cat can learn its own name. It can tell its name apart from other words, even when a stranger says it!

b1201h.text: Your dare: make your own Magnets map in TheOneApp today. Tomorrow, start a new map, and draw it again from memory. Then tap Mark my mind map. How much will you remember?

h860.text: Let's read today's key words together! Ready?
